definitions.explanation: Hard, heat-resistant material made by firing non-metallic minerals. Used of modern engineered ceramics in knives, cookware, dental work, and electronics — not of traditional pottery, which is {陶器|とうき}.

examples.japanese: セラミックの{包丁|ほうちょう}を{使|つか}っている。
この{鍋|なべ}はセラミック{加工|かこう}なので{焦|こ}げ{付|つ}きにくい。
examples.english: This pan has a ceramic coating, so food doesn't stick easily.

examples.japanese: {奥歯|おくば}の{治療|ちりょう}で、{金属|きんぞく}ではなくセラミックの{詰|つ}め{物|もの}を{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: For the treatment of my back tooth, I chose a ceramic filling rather than a metal one.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- セラミック{製|せい}: made of ceramic
- セラミック{加工|かこう}: ceramic coating
- セラミックヒーター: ceramic heater
- ファインセラミックス: fine ceramics (the industrial-materials category, usually said in the plural)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {陶器|とうき}: pottery, earthenware — traditional fired clay tableware
- {磁器|じき}: porcelain — the finer, whiter, vitrified kind
- {焼|や}き{物|もの}: ceramics, pottery — the craft and its products as a whole

Japanese takes セラミック as the modern technical word; a teacup is never described with it.
